you can try this code:
```

import gradio as gr

def on_file_change(file):
    return f"File changed: {file.name}" if file else "No file selected."

def on_file_select(file):
    return f"File selected: {file.name}" if file else "No file selected."

def on_file_upload(file):
    return f"File uploaded: {file.name}" if file else "No file uploaded."

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    file_input = gr.File(label="Upload a File")

    output_change = gr.Textbox(label="Change Event Output", interactive=True)
    output_select = gr.Textbox(label="Select Event Output", interactive=True)
    output_upload = gr.Textbox(label="Upload Event Output", interactive=True)

    file_input.change(on_file_change, inputs=file_input, outputs=output_change)
    file_input.select(on_file_select, inputs=file_input, outputs=output_select)
    file_input.upload(on_file_upload, inputs=file_input, outputs=output_upload)

demo.launch(server_port=7861)
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Oh I just went through this issue and I now understand, there's a miscommunication on the semantics of these event triggers. Sorry for not realizing earlier.

The `.upload()` event fires after a file has finished uploading, so it fires correctly for you. The `.change()` event happens after the value of the file component changes for any reason, whether programmatically or via UI interaction. The `select()` event happens after a user "selects" or clicks upon one of the files that have already been uploaded. After uploading files, you can click on them for futher action as you can see in my recording.

Hope that clears things up!

ok great!
my suggestion:
- use .rowselect or .listselect to not be confused with the JS .onselect or "select" event listener.
- .upload event should be fired like JS event does, meaning when the upload starts.
- .select event should be the same behavior of JS, meaning when the user select a file or cancel from its local filemanager
